original_value: Recording runtime status via logs is common for almost every computer system, and detecting anomalies in logs is crucial for timely identifying malfunctions of systems. However, manually detecting anomalies for logs is time-consuming, error-prone, and infeasible. Existing automatic log anomaly detection approaches, using indexes rather than semantics of log templates, tend to cause false alarms. In this work, we propose LogAnomaly, a framework to model unstructured a log stream as a natural language sequence. Empowered by template2vec, a novel, simple yet effective method to extract the semantic information hidden in log templates, LogAnomaly can detect both sequential and quantitive log anomalies simultaneously, which were not done by any previous work. Moreover, LogAnomaly can avoid the false alarms caused by the newly appearing log templates between periodic model retrainings. Our evaluation on two public production log datasets show that LogAnomaly outperforms existing log-based anomaly detection methods.

result.paraphrase: Monitoring runtime status through logs is common in nearly all computer systems, and spotting anomalies in logs is essential for detecting system malfunctions in time. Yet manual log anomaly detection is time-consuming, error-prone, and impractical. Existing automated log anomaly detection methods, which rely on indexes instead of the semantics of log templates, often produce false alarms. In this work, we present LogAnomaly, a framework that models an unstructured log stream as a natural language sequence. With template2vec, a novel, simple, yet effective way to extract the semantic information embedded in log templates, LogAnomaly can detect sequential and quantitative log anomalies at the same time, something no prior work has achieved. In addition, LogAnomaly avoids false alarms caused by newly appearing log templates between periodic model retrainings. Our evaluation on two public production log datasets shows that LogAnomaly outperforms existing log-based anomaly detection methods.
